title: Module Documentation and Problem Statement
content: The module docstring introduces Erdős Problem #278 on the maximum covering density of congruence systems. Given moduli $A = \{n_1 < \cdots < n_r\}$, choose residues $a_1, \ldots, a_r$ to maximize the density of integers $m$ satisfying $m \equiv a_i \pmod{n_i}$ for some $i$. Simpson (1986) settled the minimum density case: it is achieved when all residues are equal, yielding the inclusion-exclusion formula $\sum 1/n_i - \sum 1/\text{lcm}(n_i, n_j) + \cdots$. The maximum density question remains OPEN.
mathContext: Coverage density: $d(A, \mathbf{a}) = \lim_{N \to \infty} |\{m \in [0,N) : \exists i,\, m \equiv a_i \pmod{n_i}\}|/N$. Min density = inclusion-exclusion sum (Simpson). Max density is open.

title: Coprime LCM and CRT-Based Counting Lemmas
content: Seven private helper lemmas building the coprime case machinery. `foldl_lcm_eq_foldl_mul`: for pairwise coprime elements, $\text{lcm} = \prod$. `lcm_eq_prod_of_coprime`: lifts to `Finset.lcm`. `complement_card_single_mod`: counts non-hits in $[0, nL)$. `complement_count_two_mod`: extends to two coprime moduli via CRT. `complement_eq_prod`: for pairwise coprime moduli, complement count = $\prod(n_i - 1)$, giving coprime coverage $1 - \prod(1 - 1/n_i)$.
mathContext: For pairwise coprime $\{n_1, \ldots, n_r\}$: by CRT, $|\{m \in [0, \prod n_i) : \forall i,\, m \not\equiv a_i \pmod{n_i}\}| = \prod(n_i - 1)$. Coverage: $1 - \prod(1 - 1/n_i)$.

title: Cyclic Shift Bijection and Simpson's Minimum Density
content: Helpers proving coverage density is shift-invariant. `coverage_card_shift`: coverage for constant residue $a$ equals coverage for residue 0, via the cyclic shift $m \mapsto (m+a) \bmod L$ on $[0,L)$. Since each $n \mid L$, the shift preserves residue classes. This establishes Simpson's result: minimum coverage density is at the constant-residue system.
mathContext: Shift bijection $\phi_a(m) = (m+a) \bmod L$ preserves residue classes mod any $n \mid L$. Therefore coverage count is translation-invariant: $|\{m : \exists i, m \equiv a \pmod{n_i}\}| = |\{m : \exists i, m \equiv 0 \pmod{n_i}\}|$.

title: Imports and Setup
content: Imports Mathlib for `Finset.Card` (counting covered residues), `Nat.GCD.Basic` and `Nat.Prime.Basic` (for LCM and coprimality), `Data.Real.Basic` (for density as a real number), and tactics. The formalization works with moduli in $\mathbb{N}$ and densities in $\mathbb{R}$.
mathContext: The coverage density $\delta(\mathcal{S}) = |\{0 \leq m < L : m \text{ covered}\}| / L$ where $L = \mathrm{lcm}(n_1, \ldots, n_r)$ requires both natural number arithmetic (modular residues, LCM) and real division.

title: Congruence System
content: A congruence system consists of a finite set of moduli $\{n_1, \ldots, n_r\}$ with chosen residues $a_i$ for each modulus $n_i$. Each pair $(n_i, a_i)$ defines an arithmetic progression $\{m : m \equiv a_i \pmod{n_i}\}$. The positivity condition $n_i > 0$ ensures well-defined modular arithmetic.
mathContext: A congruence system $\mathcal{S} = \{a_i \pmod{n_i}\}_{i=1}^r$ covers $m$ if $m \equiv a_i \pmod{n_i}$ for some $i$. This is the setup for **covering systems** studied by Erdős from the 1950s onward.

title: Coverage Predicate
content: An integer $m$ is covered by the system if $m \equiv a_i \pmod{n_i}$ for at least one modulus $n_i$. This is the union of arithmetic progressions: $\bigcup_{i=1}^r \{m : m \equiv a_i \pmod{n_i}\}$.
mathContext: The coverage set is $C(\mathcal{S}) = \bigcup_{i=1}^r (a_i + n_i\mathbb{Z})$. A **covering system** has $C(\mathcal{S}) = \mathbb{Z}$ (every integer is covered). Problem #278 asks about the density $|C(\mathcal{S}) \cap [0, L)|/L$ rather than requiring full coverage.

title: LCM Period
content: The LCM of all moduli, $L = \mathrm{lcm}(n_1, \ldots, n_r)$, is the period of the coverage pattern. Coverage of $m$ depends only on $m \bmod L$, so density can be computed exactly over one period.
mathContext: Since each congruence $m \equiv a_i \pmod{n_i}$ has period $n_i$, the system has period $L = \mathrm{lcm}(n_1, \ldots, n_r)$. The density is $\delta = |\{0 \leq m < L : m \in C(\mathcal{S})\}| / L$.

title: Coverage Density
content: The coverage density $\delta(\mathcal{S})$ is the fraction of residues in $\{0, \ldots, L-1\}$ covered by at least one congruence. Since the system is periodic with period $L$, this equals the asymptotic density of covered integers. Made `noncomputable` because set membership is not decidable in general.
mathContext: $$\delta(\mathcal{S}) = \frac{|\{0 \leq m < L : \exists i, m \equiv a_i \pmod{n_i}\}|}{L}$$ where $L = \mathrm{lcm}(n_1, \ldots, n_r)$. By periodicity, $\delta$ equals the natural density $\lim_{N \to \infty} |C(\mathcal{S}) \cap [0,N)| / N$.

title: Max and Min Coverage Density
content: The maximum and minimum coverage density over all residue choices, for fixed moduli. These are the optimization targets of Problem #278: Simpson (1986) resolved the minimum, while the maximum remains open for non-coprime moduli. Uses `sSup`/`sInf` over the set of achievable densities.
mathContext: $$\delta_{\max}(A) = \sup_{a_1, \ldots, a_r} \delta(\mathcal{S}), \quad \delta_{\min}(A) = \inf_{a_1, \ldots, a_r} \delta(\mathcal{S})$$ The finite period $L$ means only finitely many distinct densities are achievable (at most $\prod n_i$ residue combinations), so the sup and inf are attained.

title: LCM Positivity Lemmas
content: Two lemmas establishing that `foldl Nat.lcm` preserves positivity (by induction on the list) and that `systemLCM` is always positive. These are needed to ensure the density denominator is nonzero. The proof uses `Nat.lcm_eq_zero_iff` to show the LCM of positive numbers is positive.
mathContext: $\mathrm{lcm}(a, b) = 0 \iff a = 0 \lor b = 0$, so $\mathrm{lcm}$ of positive numbers is positive. By induction, $\mathrm{foldl}(\mathrm{lcm}, 1, [n_1, \ldots, n_r]) > 0$ when all $n_i > 0$.

title: Density Bounds: 0 ≤ δ ≤ 1
content: Three proved results: density is non-negative (ratio of naturals), at most 1 (filtered set is a subset of the range), and the combined bound $0 \leq \delta \leq 1$. These are the only fully proved theorems in the file — everything else is axiomatized.
mathContext: $0 \leq \delta(\mathcal{S}) \leq 1$ because $0 \leq |S| \leq L$ for $S \subseteq \{0, \ldots, L-1\}$. The proof of $\delta \leq 1$ uses `div_le_one` with the cast $L > 0$ from `systemLCM_pos`.

title: Inclusion-Exclusion Density
content: The first-order inclusion-exclusion approximation $\sum_{i=1}^r 1/n_i$ for the equal-residue coverage density. The full formula is $\sum 1/n_i - \sum 1/\mathrm{lcm}(n_i, n_j) + \cdots$, but only the first term is formalized here.
mathContext: For equal residues, the coverage density is $\delta = \sum_{\emptyset \neq S \subseteq [r]} (-1)^{|S|+1} / \mathrm{lcm}_{i \in S}(n_i)$ by inclusion-exclusion on the events $\{m \equiv a \pmod{n_i}\}$. The first-order term $\sum 1/n_i$ is an upper bound (it overcounts overlaps).

title: Simpson's Theorem (1986)
content: The minimum coverage density is achieved when all residues are equal: $\delta_{\min} = \delta(\mathcal{S}_0)$ where $\mathcal{S}_0$ uses $a_i = 0$ for all $i$. Simpson's proof uses a probabilistic/averaging argument over residue shifts. The corollary `equal_residues_minimize` states that all constant-residue systems achieve the same density (shifting residues uniformly doesn't change coverage count).
mathContext: **Simpson (1986)**: $\forall r : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}, \; \delta(\{0 \pmod{n_i}\}) \leq \delta(\{r(n_i) \pmod{n_i}\})$. The proof averages over shifts: $\mathbb{E}_t[\delta(\{a_i + t \pmod{n_i}\})] = \delta(\{0 \pmod{n_i}\})$, so the minimum is at most this expectation.

title: Coprime Case: Maximum Density
content: When all moduli are pairwise coprime, the maximum coverage density is $\sum 1/n_i$, achieved by the Chinese Remainder Theorem. Coprimality means the congruences are independent: $\Pr[m \equiv a_i \pmod{n_i} \text{ and } m \equiv a_j \pmod{n_j}] = 1/(n_i n_j)$, so inclusion-exclusion simplifies to $1 - \prod(1 - 1/n_i)$.
mathContext: For pairwise coprime moduli, $\mathrm{lcm}(n_i, n_j) = n_i n_j$, so the inclusion-exclusion formula gives $\delta = 1 - \prod_{i=1}^r (1 - 1/n_i)$. By CRT, residue choices can't reduce overlap below independence, so $\delta_{\max} = \sum 1/n_i$ (when $\sum 1/n_i \leq 1$).

title: Maximum Density: The Open Problem
content: The main open part of Problem #278: what is the maximum coverage density for general (non-coprime) moduli? Axiomatized as $\delta_{\max} \leq 1$, which is trivially true but highlights that no tighter bound is known in general. Non-coprimality allows clever residue alignment to control overlap structure.
mathContext: For non-coprime moduli, $\gcd(n_i, n_j) > 1$ creates dependencies: the events $m \equiv a_i \pmod{n_i}$ and $m \equiv a_j \pmod{n_j}$ are correlated. Clever residue choices can **increase** coverage (by reducing overlap) or **decrease** it (by aligning overlaps). The optimal strategy is unknown.

title: Single Modulus Case
content: For a single modulus $n$, there is only one residue to choose, and the coverage density is exactly $1/n$ regardless of the choice. This is the trivial base case: max = min = $1/n$.
mathContext: For $|A| = 1$ with $A = \{n\}$: $\delta_{\max}(\{n\}) = \delta_{\min}(\{n\}) = 1/n$. Exactly $L/n = \mathrm{lcm}(n)/n = 1$ residue class is covered in each period, giving density $1/n$.

title: Complement Count via CRT (Main Technical Lemma)
content: The file's largest proved result (~110 lines): for pairwise coprime moduli $n_1, \ldots, n_k$, the number of integers in $[0, \prod n_i)$ not covered by the congruence system with residues $a_i$ is exactly $\prod(n_i - 1)$. The proof uses `Finset.induction` on the moduli set, with the inductive step establishing that each modulus $n$ contributes a factor of $(n-1)/n$ to the uncovered proportion via the CRT-based residue shift argument. This is the heart of the coprime density formula.
mathContext: For pairwise coprime $n_1, \ldots, n_k$: $|\{m \in [0, \prod n_i) : m \not\equiv a_i \pmod{n_i} \; \forall i\}| = \prod_{i=1}^k (n_i - 1)$. Dividing by $\prod n_i$: uncovered fraction $= \prod(1 - 1/n_i)$, so coverage density $= 1 - \prod(1 - 1/n_i)$.

title: Equal Residues Minimize Density (Simpson's Application)
content: Proves that choosing all residues equal ($a_i = a$ for all $i$) minimizes the coverage density: `equal_residues_minimize` shows $\delta(\text{sys}_{\text{all-}a}) \leq \delta(\text{sys})$ for any system. This uses `simpson_theorem` (axiomatized): Simpson proved that the minimum density over all residue choices equals $1 - \prod(1 - 1/n_i)$, achieved exactly when all residues are equal (maximizing overlaps between congruence classes).
mathContext: $\delta_{\min}(n_1, \ldots, n_k) = 1 - \prod_{i=1}^k (1 - 1/n_i)$, achieved by $a_1 = a_2 = \cdots = a_k = a$ (any common $a$). Equal residues maximize overlaps between arithmetic progressions.

title: Coprime Density Formula: All Residue Choices Give Same Density
content: `coprime_density_formula`: for **pairwise coprime** moduli, every choice of residues gives the same coverage density $1 - \prod(1 - 1/n_i)$. This is the CRT uniformity result: when moduli are coprime, the covering pattern is determined solely by the moduli (not the residues), because CRT gives a bijection between residue tuples and elements of $\mathbb{Z}/\prod n_i$. The proof uses `complement_count_coprime` to show uncovered count is $\prod(n_i-1)$ regardless of residues.
mathContext: For coprime $n_1, \ldots, n_k$: $\delta(a_1, \ldots, a_k) = 1 - \prod(1 - 1/n_i)$ for ALL choices of $a_i$. Equivalently: $\delta_{\max} = \delta_{\min} = 1 - \prod(1 - 1/n_i)$.

title: Coprime Moduli: Max = Min Density
content: `coprime_max_eq_min`: for pairwise coprime moduli, the maximum and minimum coverage densities coincide. This is a direct corollary of `coprime_density_formula` — if all residue choices give the same density, then the supremum and infimum over choices are trivially equal. This makes the non-coprime case the interesting one for Problem #278.
mathContext: Coprime $\Rightarrow$ $\delta_{\max}(n_1, \ldots, n_k) = \delta_{\min}(n_1, \ldots, n_k) = 1 - \prod(1 - 1/n_i)$. The gap $\delta_{\max} - \delta_{\min} > 0$ only occurs for non-coprime moduli.

title: Singleton and Single-Modulus Density Results
content: Three results for the simplest cases: `singleton_coverage_density` proves $\delta(\{n\}, a) = 1/n$ for any modulus $n$ and residue $a$. `single_modulus_density` proves max = min = $1/n$ for a single modulus. These establish the base case from which the general coprime density formula builds by induction.
mathContext: For $k = 1$: $\delta(\{n\}) = 1/n$, $\delta_{\max}(\{n\}) = \delta_{\min}(\{n\}) = 1/n$. The formula $1 - (1 - 1/n) = 1/n$ matches.
